one_liner: CivicState turns civic complaints into paid, citation-backed official letters, but demand is unproven.

authority.quorum: POM soul-review plus wrk.dog merge constitute adoption; operator must confirm whether this personal/research asset should pitch as a business.
authority.decisionRecord: POM soul-review + wrk.dog merge constitute adoption - operator ruling 2026-06-12; see the PR's POM record.
authority.rationale: The artifact is intentionally needs-revision because market demand, deliverability, official coverage, legal posture, and project identity remain unvalidated.

pomReviews.summary: Created a VC-grade plan from workspace evidence, but blocked approval pending operator and market validation.

research.summary: Workspace-only review found a CivicState prototype with substantial implementation code and planning files, but no real customer, payment, deliverability, coverage, or legal-review evidence.
methods: Read repo planning corpus and source files.
Separated implemented prototype evidence from market assumptions.
Built bottom-up sizing from price and assumed transaction counts because network research was unavailable.
Preserved contradictions in a Surprise Spikes section instead of smoothing them.

planningMethod.evidenceHarvest: Use repo planning files, package metadata, source routes, worker agents, Prisma schema, and tests as evidence of what exists.
planningMethod.marketResearch: No network research was available; all external market, competitor, and valuation claims are marked as assumptions.
planningMethod.financialValidation: Revenue is modeled as paid submissions times blended ARPU from code pricing, with variable and fixed costs labeled as assumptions unless tied to repo files.
planningMethod.alternativeSearch: Compared the current B2C paid-letter path against free manual outreach, petitions, Resistbot-style messaging, and enterprise advocacy software as assumption-labeled substitutes.
planningMethod.antiPlan: Attacked willingness to pay, deliverability, legal-adjacent citation risk, official data coverage, and project identity before allowing roadmap authority.
planningMethod.finalSynthesis: Keep CivicState as a validation-gated research asset until operator confirms business posture and market proof clears.

segments.name: U.S. residents with specific civic issues
segments.painfulJob: They need a researched, citation-backed letter sent to the correct officials without doing jurisdiction, law, and contact research themselves.

segments.name: Repeat local advocates
segments.painfulJob: They need professional official outreach that is more credible than generic emails or petitions.

currentSubstitutes: Manual search and direct email to officials.
Government complaint portals and phone calls.
Petition platforms and local advocacy groups.
Enterprise advocacy tools used by organizations rather than individual citizens.
willingnessToPayEvidence: The repo implements $5, $15, and $25 pricing tiers.
The planning files require a >=3% paid conversion validation gate.
No real willingness-to-pay evidence was found in workspace.

market.category: Consumer civic-tech transaction workflow for citation-backed official letters.
market.competitiveLandscape: Substitutes include free manual outreach, government portals, petition platforms, Resistbot-style messaging, and enterprise advocacy platforms such as Quorum or VoterVoice; all external competitor claims are assumptions in this workspace-only run.
market.wedge: Start with paid, preview-led individual campaigns where correct official targeting and verified citations create visible value before payment.

businessModel.valueCreation: Collapse issue description, official targeting, legal/citation research, drafting, moderation, payment, and delivery into one workflow.
businessModel.valueDelivery: Web app plus Express API and BullMQ worker agents using Clerk, Stripe, Postmark, Prisma, and legal data integrations in the current prototype.
businessModel.valueCapture: Transactional fees per campaign at $5, $15, and $25 tiers.
businessModel.pricing: $5 single official, $15 three-pack, $25 full-spread as implemented in apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts.
businessModel.revenuePath: Validate B2C paid submissions first; defer organization/API revenue until citizen pipeline is stable.
businessModel.unitEconomics: Assumed blended ARPU is $13.00 with assumed $0.45 variable cost and assumed 96.5% gross margin before fixed/vendor costs.
businessModel.operatingCosts: DigitalOcean/Vercel infrastructure, local official data provider, Postmark, Stripe, legal/compliance review, support, moderation, and model usage.
businessModel.marginLogic: Margins hold only if operator review stays low, deliverability works, local data costs do not overwhelm low ticket sizes, and citation QA avoids expensive manual review.

financialModel.summary: Three-year validation model: 1,200 submissions in Y1, 6,000 in Y2, and 18,000 in Y3 at $13.00 blended ARPU, all assumption-labeled.
financialModel.validationStatus: Needs market validation; not approved as a production forecast.
revenueAssumptions: 40% of paid campaigns choose $5 single, 40% choose $15 three-pack, and 20% choose $25 full-spread.
Paid conversion must clear the repo's >=3% validation gate before growth work.
No subscription or enterprise revenue is included in the first three years.
costAssumptions: Variable AI and delivery cost averages $0.45 per submission.
Fixed/vendor/op costs are $8,400 in Y1, $24,000 in Y2, and $72,000 in Y3.
Local official data may cost $100-$500 per month and remains a major unknown.
sensitivityTests: If blended ARPU falls to $8.00, Y3 revenue falls to $144,000 on 18,000 submissions.
If conversion is 1.0% rather than >=3%, acquisition and value proposition must be reworked.
If deliverability is below 70%, email-first delivery should pause and alternate channels must be evaluated.

alternatives.name: Manual outreach and portals
alternatives.thesis: Free manual workflows remain the strongest substitute if users do not value research and drafting enough to pay.
alternatives.expectedUpside: No vendor or product risk for the user.
alternatives.financialCase: CivicState must beat free with speed, accuracy, and official targeting at a $5-$25 price point.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Rejected as the product path, but retained as the main competitive threat.

alternatives.name: Enterprise advocacy platform
alternatives.thesis: Organizations already pay for advocacy software, but that is not the current individual-citizen wedge.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Higher contract values if the product eventually pivots B2B.
alternatives.financialCase: Could support subscriptions, but would require sales, onboarding, and compliance scope absent from the current code.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Deferred until the citizen pipeline proves demand.

alternatives.name: Research-only civic assistant
alternatives.thesis: The asset could remain a personal/research tool rather than a paid business.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Lower legal, deliverability, and chargeback risk.
alternatives.financialCase: No meaningful near-term revenue, but preserves reusable code and research value.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Still plausible because registry notes say personal/research asset.

antiPlan.summary: CivicState can fail if willingness to pay, deliverability, legal posture, official data quality, or operator identity does not clear.

holes.hole: Users may not pay for something they can send manually for free.
holes.whyItMatters: Without paid conversion, the product has no business model despite polished automation.
holes.repair: Run paid preview-to-checkout beta and stop growth work if conversion misses the repo's >=3% gate.

holes.hole: Government email deliverability may be poor.
holes.whyItMatters: If letters do not reach inboxes, the delivery promise fails.
holes.repair: Use domain warming, Postmark webhooks, bounce thresholds, and beta deliverability audits before launch claims.

holes.hole: Citation-backed drafting may create legal-adjacent risk.
holes.whyItMatters: The product must not be mistaken for legal advice or legal filings.
holes.repair: Require legal/operator review of disclaimers, AI disclosure, citation verification, and human review boundaries.

holes.hole: Local official data may be incomplete or expensive.
holes.whyItMatters: Bad routing undermines the core value and paid data vendors can overwhelm small-ticket economics.
holes.repair: Run a ZIP coverage audit before broad local-official claims.

mitigations: Keep status needs-revision until operator merge.
Use paid beta and deliverability tests as near-term gates.
Separate evidence from assumptions in all investor-facing claims.
Treat current direct Clerk/Stripe/Postmark rails as prototype if WrkPlug becomes authoritative.
residualRisks: Operator may decide not to pitch this asset as a business.
External competitors and legal rules were not live-researched.
A working repo may still have no repeatable distribution.
Manual review may break unit economics at low ticket sizes.

strategy.diagnosis: The repo has implementation momentum but lacks market proof and has contradictory planning state.
strategy.guidingPolicy: Do not add speculative product scope; validate paid demand, delivery, coverage, and legal posture first.
strategy.whereToPlay: Individual U.S. civic issues where email-to-official is acceptable and citations improve credibility.
strategy.howToWin: Show a high-quality preview before payment, target the correct officials, verify citations, and track delivery status.
strategy.moatHypothesis: Verified official data, bounce/response history, reusable citations, compliance/audit logs, and opt-in public campaign pages could compound after real volume.
tradeoffs: No broad social/petition feature expansion before paid workflow proof.
No investor pitch until operator confirms this is a business.
No claim of approved roadmap authority while status is needs-revision.

channels: Local issue communities and civic newsletters.
Opt-in SEO campaign pages after compliance review.
assumptions: Users will trust AI-assisted letters if disclosure and citations are visible.
Organic search can compound if public pages are safe and useful.

jobs: Monitor delivery bounces and spam complaints.
Maintain official suppression and opt-out list.
aiNativeAutomationTargets: Flag risky content for human review.

aiWorkGovernance.wedge: AI assists research and drafting but must be bounded by citation verification, moderation, audit logs, and human review.
aiWorkGovernance.problem: Unverified civic/legal claims and unsafe messages can create trust, deliverability, and legal-adjacent risk.
aiWorkGovernance.promise: Every delivered letter should carry verified citations, disclosure, moderation status, and auditability.
duplicatePrevention: Use root BUSINESS.md as the canonical plan.
Use ROADMAP.md Buildable Next Work as the next-work source.
Use DECISIONS.md to record operator rulings and validation outcomes.
tokenSpendControls: Human review when all citations fail.
aiWorkGovernance.risk: AI output is not evidence; generated letters must not be treated as legal advice or market validation.

regulatory: CAN-SPAM posture, AI disclosure, not-legal-advice disclaimer, opt-out handling, and privacy rights require review before launch claims.
privacy: Political opinion and civic issue text are sensitive personal data and should remain encrypted or deleted according to policy.
security: Audit logs, ledger entries, HMAC checksums, and app-level encryption are part of the repo posture.
brand: Project identity conflict between brooks-history and CivicState must be resolved before pitching.
operational: No 24/7 staffing; routine operator work must remain exception-based.

killTriggers: Paid conversion below 3% after a representative beta.
Legal/operator review rejects the citation-backed consumer-letter posture.
pivotTriggers: B2C users will not pay but organizations request workflow access.
Email delivery fails but certified mail/fax has demand.
Research assistant usage is high but delivery is low.
reviseTriggers: Local official data provider is too expensive or inaccurate.
Operator decides the asset remains personal/research only.
wakeConditions: Paid beta records real checkout attempts.
Delivery and coverage evidence is available.

experiments.question: Will users pay?
experiments.method: Run 20 concierge beta checkout attempts at existing tiers.
experiments.successSignal: Conversion at or above the repo's >=3% gate with clear reasons from non-buyers.

experiments.question: Can letters reach officials?
experiments.method: Run domain-warmed beta sends and inspect Postmark/inbox outcomes.

experiments.question: Is official matching good enough?
experiments.method: Audit 25 ZIP codes against manual federal, state, and local official lists.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Users will pay $5-$25 for a citation-backed letter workflow.
assumptionLedger.evidence: Pricing exists in apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts, but no customer proof was found.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Run paid beta and capture declined-checkout reasons.

assumptionLedger.assumption: Email-first delivery is enough for the initial product.
Citation verification can keep quality and legal-adjacent risk manageable.
Local official data can be acquired economically.
assumptionLedger.evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md says Cicero/BallotReady evaluation is needed and may cost $100-$500/month.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Run provider evaluation and ZIP coverage audit.

assumptionLedger.assumption: SEO can become a low-CAC channel.
assumptionLedger.evidence: .planning/GENESIS.md states the SEO hypothesis; no traffic evidence was found.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Publish opt-in compliant pages and measure impressions.

assumptionLedger.assumption: WrkPlug shared rails lower long-term infra and CAC.
assumptionLedger.evidence: Brief requires WrkPlug client posture; current code uses direct Clerk/Stripe/Postmark.
assumptionLedger.challenge: Operator confirms WrkPlug Phase 0 and migration boundary.
